column3: The ticker polls for a real public proof child file; success requires the published file or the exact child result.

The frozen corpus phase deadline is the package deadline less a cleanup reserve, so a real engine build or worker that overruns fails naming its phase instead of the package timeout panicking in TempDir removal; it never paces a passing run.
Both deadlines are fixed in the past to test cancellation propagation and never wait.

Support file: FakeGuardedNetwork's one-second dial context is the fake runtime's own probe of an allowed loopback port; the only caller sends a denied envelope, which returns before any dial, so no test waits on it.
The pause polls a real ACP stub's journal for the sent prompt before the signal; success requires the observed wire record.
Support file: after the fake round sends itself SIGKILL it parks in a sleep loop so it cannot run on to a plain exit before the signal lands; nothing is timed and nothing is decided by the wait.

One pause paces a goroutine that waits for the hold's argv and ends with its run; one sleep is the artificial clock's yield to the supervisor's goroutines; one 50ms window is a negative check that only a supervisor exiting while its hold lives can fail, and a slow host can only make it pass.
Both pauses poll a real ACP stub's journal and outcome files; success requires the observed wire records.

One pause paces reaping a released supervisor and one lets a real Follow reach the log's end before a line is appended; the elapsed check on a supervisor that died before readiness belongs to the readiness-as-event slice (cluster E part 2), which replaces it.
The one deadline caps the join of an in-process supervisor owning a real fixture application, failing the test rather than hanging it; success requires the observed record, signals and group reads.

Support file: time.After is the default of the fake channel server's injectable long-poll clock, and the 100ms ticker paces a poll for a test's pause file that ends on the file or the request's context, never on elapsed time.
The sleeping child is the stop fixture's subject and is killed, never waited out.
Support file: the custodian's system clock, the production side of the injected custodianClock seam (After, AfterFunc and Sleep); tests drive the custodian through a fake clock.
The one reading labels each witness snapshot with the time into its wait for diagnosis; every wait ends on its witness event, and the label decides nothing.
The scans observe real kernel process membership and end on the survivor fact; the two pauses only space the scans and bound nothing.
Real sleep paces the concurrent supervisor cancellation test; the timer caps observation of its terminal result.
The pause polls a real ACP stub's journal for the sent prompt before the signal; success requires the observed wire record.
A TERM the ignore-term hold ignores leaves no event to wait on: the 300ms pause gives a hold that wrongly honours TERM the time to show it, and a slow host can only make the check pass, never fail.
Three tickers pace polls of custody barrier files, a watchdog record and an exact process's terminal state; each ends on the fact, the command's end or the test's context, never on elapsed time.
Deadlines prove denial while native host-slot owners live; the sleeping helper is a subject killed by the test.
Three pauses pace polls of a helper's ready and pid files inside the subprocess helpers; each ends on the files, never on elapsed time.
Two pollers read emitted output while the suite runs; every wait ends on the barrier, the launcher returning or the test context, never elapsed time.
The helper child runs the production steward loop on the real clock (time.Sleep passed as its Sleep); the test's own waits are its witness events.
Two hour-long sleeps keep fixture subject processes alive until the test kills them; nothing is timed.

Support file: Await, the one wait every converted test uses: a 10ms pause between observations of a fact, and one reading of the time left before the test binary's own deadline (go test -timeout), where it gives up naming what it awaited.

Support file, not converted (reported): the fixture process-group reaper bounds orderly cleanups and the post-SIGKILL group exit wait with deadlines scaled from the fixture custodian's bound, and its contract tests require them; making them unbounded event waits is a change to the fixture custody design.
The context is passed to a fake that checks for a deadline and returns immediately without waiting.

Support file, not converted (reported): after the test binary's survivors are SIGKILLed, the exit scan waits for each exit within the scaled fixture exit bound and only reports when it expires; the binary already fails for the survivor, so the bound decides nothing.

Support file, not converted (reported): the process fixture's teardown and AwaitExactExit wait for a SIGKILLed child's exit within the scaled fixture exit bound and its key scan polls on a ticker until its context ends; making the exit waits unbounded is a change to the fixture custody design and its failure-path tests.
Support file: the fake ACP agent's scripted pause between streamed chunks, which a cancellation or teardown ends at once; it is the fake's behaviour, not a test's wait.
The ticker spaces fixture writes, and all assertions count samples only after the writer reports completion.
